title: Soft Grant Orchestrator and Anticipatory Decommit for Dedicated Fleets
author: Maya Chen
release_notes:
- Introduces Soft Grant Orchestrator to allow temporary capacity grants for tenants, reducing long-running reservations.
- Adds anticipatory decommit logic to trim excess reservations during sustained underutilization.
- New telemetry stream for per-tenant granted vs used capacity exposed to Console.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets currently rely on hard reservations and long-lived commitments to guarantee tenant throughput. This leads to headroom waste when tenants have bursty behavior and to conservative sizing.

This PR introduces the Soft Grant Orchestrator (SGO): a transient-grant mechanism that allows the autoscaler to issue short-lived capacity grants to tenants for burst windows, together with an anticipatory decommit path that gently reduces long-lived reservations when sustained underutilization is detected. The goal is to preserve percentile throughput guarantees while reducing committed GPU hours.

What changed (high-level):
- New controller: controllers/soft_grant_orchestrator.go — issues grants with TTL and backoff, tracks grant health and fallbacks.
- Reservation reconciler: modified to respect soft grants and to annotate reservations with "grant-origin" for observability.
- Anticipatory decommit module: heuristics that analyze a rolling 1h utilization window and schedule step-downs with a safety fence and cooldown.
- Telemetry pipeline: exporters/tenant_grant_telemetry.go publishes granted_vs_used, grant_ttl, and anticipated_decommit_reason into the existing metrics pipeline and a compact one-minute histogram for Console.
- Tests: unit + e2e harness changes to simulate bursty traffic and verify SLA preservation under grant/trim cycles.

Design notes and safety:
- Grants are additive and ephemeral; the orchestrator never revokes hard reservations. If capacity pressure is detected the scheduler will automatically fall back to hard-reserved capacity.
- Anticipatory decommit only trims up to 25% of a tenant's reservation per step and requires a 30m low-utilization confirmation window before enacting. A short safety hold (10m) prevents immediate re-provisioning churn.
- We added an emergency opt-out label (dedicated.sgo/opt-out=true) for tenants that want deterministic reservation behavior.

Migration / rollout plan:
1) Deploy SGO disabled by feature flag. Monitor telemetry for false positives.
2) Enable SGO for a small cohort (internal "pilot" tenants) for 48h and validate no SLA regressions.
3) Gradually scale to controlled percentage of fleets.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for orchestrator state machine and decommit gating.
- Synthetic load canaries included in perf-canary to exercise grant issuance and backstop fallback.
- Benchmarks show <3% additional scheduler latency on grant decision path under 95th percentile load.

Related: Linear ENG-2145 implements the product acceptance criteria; SUP-4432 captured customer request to reduce overcommit in monthly billings.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can we make the 25% step configurable per-fleet? Some enterprise customers have tighter burst constraints.

Ravi Kumar: The 1h rolling window seems aggressive for tenants with diurnal patterns. Suggest an adaptive window or minimum sample count.
Maya Chen: Switched gating to require at least 3 low-utilization windows in the last 2 hours (configurable) before action. Added tests to cover diurnal mock traces.
Elena Sokolov: Telemetry will double-count when grants overlap with autoscaler actions; confirm metrics alignment with existing reservation gauge.
Maya Chen: Exporter now emits a grant_delta metric and uses reservation UID to dedupe; updated mapping to Console charts.
